speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To better understand your symptoms, could you tell me if you have noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, and have you experienced any dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of jaundice, dark urine, or pale stools? Given your ulcerative colitis, I need to rule out Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, so I will also check for any abdominal pain or fever.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and the presence of scleral icterus, I suspect Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP is normal, Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis is unlikely. Given your sexual history, I need to rule out viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B and C serology

speaker: Doctor
text: With PSC and viral hepatitis ruled out, I need to investigate autoimmune causes. REQUEST TEST: Antimitochondrial antibody (AMA) and antinuclear antibody (ANA)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Antinuclear Antibody (ANA): Negative; Antimitochondrial Antibodies (AMA): Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: With AMA and ANA negative, we must rule out IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis and autoimmune hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Serum IgG4 levels and liver biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text: With autoimmune causes and PSC ruled out, I need to check for other cholestatic conditions. REQUEST TEST: Alkaline Phosphatase and GGT levels

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Alkaline Phosphatase: 460 U/L; GGT: Not provided in data

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly elevated Alkaline Phosphatase confirms a cholestatic pattern, but the normal MRCP and negative autoimmune serologies are puzzling. Have you noticed any weight loss, night sweats, or bone pain, and do you have any personal or family history of lymphoma or other malignancies?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, Ulcerative Colitis Social history: Sexually active with inconsistent condom use

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the cholestatic pattern and negative workup for common causes, I need to rule out malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CT scan of abdomen and pelvis
